answer: Each agent may spend only credits earned from completed work to bid for new tasks, and a contract pays only after an independent reviewer confirms delivery. A basalt ledger records each credit’s source and prevents the same reward from being claimed twice; a vertex that repeatedly approves linked accounts loses its review bond. An attacker can still create many identities, but must fund each with real work or scarce stake, while coordinated approvals risk forfeiting that stake, making a cheap Sybil swarm costly to sustain. The ledge is that colluding reviewers can still miss fabricated work.
